title: Training Note — The Stretch the Repricing Review Reads on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Training Note — The Stretch the Repricing Review Reads on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

*Basis questions answered for the finance desk.*

**What is the stretch?** It is the run of whole calendar months over which the missed cycles on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan are counted when the plan is being settled.

**How long does it run?**

- Where the plan has been billing for fewer whole calendar months than the term's repricing review length, the stretch runs back to the date the plan began billing, so every cycle since billing began is read.
- Where the plan has been billing for at least the term's repricing review length and stands past due at the handling date, the stretch runs twice the term's repricing review length of whole calendar months back from the handling date.
- In every other case, the stretch runs the term's repricing review length of whole calendar months back from the handling date.

**What is twice the review length?** Twice is a multiple of **2** applied to the term's repricing review length.

**What is the review length for each term?**

| Term | 6-Month Deferred Interest | 12-Month Deferred Interest | 18-Month Deferred Interest | 24-Month Equal Payment | 36-Month Equal Payment | 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repricing review length, whole months | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 12 | 12 |

**Worked examples (hypothetical).** A plan on the 12-Month Deferred Interest Plan, whose review length is 6 whole months, that has been billing for 4 whole calendar months: the stretch runs back to the date the plan began billing and reads 4 months. The same plan after 9 whole months of billing, standing past due: the stretch runs twice 6, that is 12 whole calendar months, back from the handling date. The same plan after 9 whole months of billing, standing active: the stretch runs 6 whole calendar months back from the handling date. A plan on the 48-Month Bridal Equal Payment Plan, whose review length is 12 whole months, standing past due after 20 whole months of billing: the stretch runs 24 whole calendar months back from the handling date.
